newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire ex-ambassador in French manslaughter trial.
newsitem.headline: Zaire ex-ambassador in French manslaughter trial.

text.p: Zaire's former ambassador to Paris will stand trial from Tuesday for the manslaughter of two boys in a traffic accident on the French Riviera, justice sources said on Monday.
Ex-envoy Ramazani Baya, who returned to France in January without diplomatic immunity, has been ordered to face a court in Nice on charges of manslaughter aggravated by unsafe and careless conduct.
The charge carries a penalty of up to three years in prison and a 500,000 franc ($88,000) fine.

Baya was on his way to visit President Mobutu Sese Seko, recuperating from cancer therapy at his Riviera villa, when he hit Raphael Lenoir, 13, and Ronald Lehartel, 12, on a pedestrian crossing in the Mediterranean resort of Menton on November 23.
Police have said he was driving at more than twice the legal speed limit.
Mobutu said Baya had been relieved of his ambassadorial duties but Baya said he had resigned so he could face a court in France and clear his conscience.
Relatives and neighbours of the two boys had demonstrated to demand that he be brought to justice, and the French government had asked Zaire to lift his diplomatic immunity so he could face trial.

A spokesman for the demonstrators said they would be present at the trial "in a calm and dignified manner" and urged local people to lay bunches of white flowers on the steps of the law courts. ($ = 5.70 French Francs)
